intervals.label: operation at Fermilab (NuMI/MINOS tunnel)
intervals.note: Year precision ('early in 2005'). The Science paper reports 'the first period of operation'; no end of operation is published.
intervals.quote: Early in 2005 we installed a chamber containing 1.5 kg of CF3 I, an industrial refrigerant commonly used as a fire extinguisher, at the 350-foot depth of the NuMI (Neutrinos at the Main Injector) tunnel in Fermilab.

intervals.label: completed (successor chamber took over the pressure vessel)
intervals.note: The end of the 2 kg chamber's own operation is not published. The 4 kg chamber reused its pressure vessel and first ran on 19 August 2009 (arXiv:1008.3518), so it cannot have run later than that; the last source showing the 2 kg chamber operating is the April 2008 Science paper.
intervals.quote: The COUPP 4 kg bubble chamber was the first such improvement, employing a larger synthetic fused silica bell jar inside the same pressure vessel used for the 2 kg chamber.

placements.note: Fermilab main-campus point (a surface campus marker, not surveyed); the chamber sat at the 350-foot depth of the NuMI tunnel (MINOS near-detector hall).

summary.plain: A small room-temperature jar of superheated CF3I that records bubbles with cameras; a nuclear recoil from a WIMP could trigger a bubble.
summary.technical: 1.5 kg CF3I, natural-quartz bell jar, cameras; built at the University of Chicago, operated in the NuMI/MINOS tunnel at Fermilab; pressure vessel reused for COUPP-4kg.
